content.title: How the Warriors stunned the Clippers behind a vintage Stephen Curry performance
content.text: Follow our live coverage of the NBA Play-In Tournament with the 76ers, Warriors advancing as Maxey, Curry shineSteph Curry dropped 35 points to stun the Clippers, extend the Warriors' season. Getty ImagesNBA Play-In Tournament — LatestThe NBA Play-In Tournament continued Wednesday with the 76ers clinching a playoff berth and the Warriors extending their season.Behind 31 points from Tyrese Maxey, Philadelphia advanced to the postseason with a 109-97 win over Orlando despite a 34-point night from Desmond Bane. The Sixers will face the No. 2 Boston Celtics in the first round. The Magic will face the Charlotte Hornets on Friday with the winner earning the final playoff spot in the East.Later in the night, Golden State overcame a double-digit deficit to stun the Los Angeles Clippers at the Intuit Dome as Steph Curry overcame a slow first half and injury concerns to drop 34 points in a vintage performance, including a game-winning 3-pointer in the final minute. Al Horford made four 3s in the second half alone and Draymond Green was spectacular defensively, blanketing Kawhi Leonard and totaling four steals. The Warriors will now face the Phoenix Suns on Friday with the winner becoming the No. 8 seed in the West.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRemaining Play-In Tournament schedule Two games remain in the Play-In Tournament.These two decide the final two playoff spots, the eighth seeds in the Eastern and Western conferences. The Charlotte Hornets and Orlando Magic will battle at 7:30 p.m. ET.For the nightcap, it’s the Warriors, tonight’s victors, who will play on the road and face the Suns. A fun Friday of basketball ahead.WATCH: Highlights from Warriors-ClippersYour browser does not support the video tag.Check out a couple key plays from tonight’s Warriors-Clippers game, including Steph Curry’s CLUTCH go-ahead 3.31% Picked756 votes69% PickedPorzingis shows what he's capable of with WarriorsKristaps Porzingis has struggled to find consistency — both on the floor and because of ongoing health issues — during his brief stint with the Warriors.On Wednesday night, he turned in his best performance in a Golden State uniform, finishing with 20 points, five rebounds and five assists in 28 minutes in the Warriors’ 126-121 comeback win over the LA Clippers. He was the offensive difference-maker the Warriors envisioned when they acquired him from the Atlanta Hawks just before February’s trade deadline in exchange for Jonathan Kuminga and Buddy Hield.Porzingis played with an extra bounce in his step throughout the night, moving with more purpose on both ends and his teammates fed off that energy. Porzingis’ presence helped stabilize key stretches as Golden State chipped away at a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit.He wasn’t alone. Curry scored 16 of his 35 points in the third quarter to keep the Warriors within reach, and Al Horford — Porzingis’ former teammate in Boston — added four fourth-quarter 3-pointers, finishing with 14 points.But for a team still searching for reliable support around its core, this was the version of Porziņģis the Warriors have been waiting on.It took 15 games, but he arrived when they needed him most.Readers share views on Warriors' comeback victoryThe Athletic's readers provided their takes on the Warriors' 126-121 victory over the Clippers to advance in the Play-in Tournament:Clippers choke in play-in again Getty ImagesJust as they did twice in 2022, the Clippers let another one slip away — this time against a Golden State team that finished the regular season with five more losses.The Clippers led by 13 with 9:53 remaining. But the game never felt secure.Kawhi Leonard couldn’t rest, logging just 7:45 off the floor; the Clippers were outscored by 11 in that time. Darius Garland, the team’s secondary star, was targeted relentlessly, eventually fouling out after picking up his fifth foul in the third quarter. Garland logged just 31:08, and the Clippers were outscored by nine points with him on the floor.This wasn’t just a missed opportunity. It was a familiar one.For a team that spent much of the season trying to recover from a 13-losses-in-15-games stretch in November, the ending felt appropriate. It was simply an unserious performance at the hands of a team that showed the toughness and poise to keep playing instead of waiting for a win to come.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMathurin did his part Getty ImagesIn a losing effort, Bennedict Mathurin led the Clippers in scoring off the bench and nearly helped his squad extend their season before the veteran poise of the Warriors stole the show.He dropped 23 points in 30 minutes, going 7-of-11 from the field and 5-of-6 from distance, not to mention three boards, two assists and three steals. It will be intriguing to monitor what the future holds for Mathurin in Los Angeles moving forward.Overheard from a scout on press row...“F--! OKC gets another lottery pick.”Unreal charge from Warriors Getty ImagesThe Golden State Warriors...Scored FORTY-ONE AMERICAN POINTS in the last 9:53 of tonight's game.An absolutely flammable performance.Kawhi Leonard had two 4th-quarter points, and they were irrelevant (dunk with 16.9 seconds left).Warriors eyeing a return to playoffs Getty ImagesIn Steph Curry’s career, he’s reached the NBA Playoffs 10 times. Win on Friday night against the Suns and the Warriors have reached the playoffs in back-to-back seasons. It will be Curry’s 11th career playoff appearance. It would be truly remarkable given he's 38 and still playing at a clutch level. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGui, KP step up Getty ImagesYes, Steph Curry’s heater and Draymond Green’s fourth-quarter defense were huge storylines tonight but don’t forget about the contributions of Kristaps Porzingis and Gui Santos.The duo combined for 40 points, made five 3s and shot 17-of-25 from the field. While Curry was cold in the first half, both players were critical in steadying the ship whether it was Santos punishing Darius Garland down low or Porzingis flying in for putback dunks. These winning plays continued in the second half too and were essential to the Warriors impressive road win.Horford 4-4 from 3-point range in fourth quarter Getty ImagesAl Horford struggled for the first three quarters of the Warriors’ play-in matchup against the Clippers, making him an unlikely candidate to emerge as one of Golden State’s heroes. During the third quarter, I wrote during the game:💬 "Horford has more turnovers (two) than made field goals (one) and has missed all three of his 3-pointers. He’s also a staggering -26 in +/-!”What started as a tough watch exploded into a vintage Horford performance down the stretch. Horford made his first 3-pointer of the night with 5:37 remaining, hit another from the left corner at the 4:43 mark… and another on the Warriors’ next possession from the opposite corner. That hot streak pulled the Warriors within two points of the Clippers.And that wasn’t all! Horford hit a fourth triple to give Golden State its first lead of the second half with 2:12 remaining. Horford’s four 3-point makes in the fourth quarter – in four attempts – were crucial in keeping the Warriors’ season alive in a 126-121 victory.Draymond did it again Getty ImagesThat’s the prototypical Draymond Green performance.Playing 35 minutes, the veteran forward stuffed the statsheet with seven points on 3-of-5 shooting, nine assists, six rebounds and four steals. His defense was particularly critical in the fourth quarter though, helping hold Kawhi Leonard scoreless in the frame until the last minute and registering two clutch steals that clinched the Warriors win.In fact, he appeared to injure his knee in the final minutes but gutted through the discomfort and made big plays while doing so.The Thunder already won?With the Clippers' loss tonight, the Thunder will now have a lottery pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. It’s one of the final picks owed to Oklahoma City via the Paul George trade in 2019, which as you may remember also included reigning NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.Curry on Friday's game against Suns: 'Stick with it'Steph Curry spoke on the Prime broadcast about what the Warriors will need against Phoenix:"The same resiliency. … These win-or go-home scenarios, we think we know the team, but you have to withstand the runs and stay in it emotionally. It was back and forth the whole game. Stick with it, know it’s not going to be perfect, but try to find a way to win."SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCurry on his return: 'I just love to play basketball' Steph Curry on the Prime broadcast on his return from injury:“I know I was only out for two months, but it was a difficult two months because I didn’t know on a day-to-day how I was going to feel. I thought I was going to be out 4 to 8 [months]… I just love to play basketball. When I‘m out here and get to do what I am here to do, I’m blessed.”Chris Paul sounds off @cp3 / InstagramFrom Chris Paul, unceremoniously cut by the Clippers midway through this past season...A chance to face OKCTen years, ago, Steph Curry and the Warriors faced the Oklahoma City Thunder on Feb. 27, 2016. It was an epic regular season game, culminating with an iconic Curry performance. He scored 46 points that night, with the exclamation mark being his iconic 3-pointer from beyond 30 feet in overtime with 0.6 seconds left. It’s the game that elevated Curry to superstar status in basketball. Now, 10 years later, the 38-year-old has a chance to face the Thunder in the first round of the playoffs, should the Warriors beat the Phoenix Suns on Friday night. Curry on Horford: 'I'm loving the confidence'Steph Curry on the Prime broadcast on Al Horford's fourth quarter performance:"I’m loving the confidence. He’s been doing it when he’s been available and healthy all year and his whole career. You can tell, there’s no hesitation. … It was beautiful to watch. No disrespect to the Clippers, they’re a great organization. It was amazing, when he was making those shots, what the energy in this arena turned into. That’s what the NBA’s about.”
